question: For experimental grouped-Claw updates, should a single exact `planIntegrity` acknowledgment be allowed to authorize both ordinary content changes and disclosed capability escalations, or must capability escalations have a distinct consent contract?
rationale: The planner’s serialized API and the follow-on executor will establish the user and host consent model; source-level review cannot safely choose that product/security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require distinct capability consent
options.body: Keep the integrity token for binding the full plan, but model and require a separately explicit capability-escalation acknowledgement in the host/apply contract.

options.title: Approve one bound acknowledgement
options.body: Document that one exact plan-integrity acknowledgement intentionally approves both content and capability changes because each escalation is structurally disclosed.

recommendation.title: Require distinct capability consent
recommendation.body: Keep the integrity token for binding the full plan, but model and require a separately explicit capability-escalation acknowledgement in the host/apply contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned to the PR and has already reviewed the surrounding planning and ownership contract in detail.
